previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex medical history including acute myeloid leukemia in remission after bone marrow transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 10%, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, and sarcoidosis, was readmitted due to recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. He had been discharged recently after treatment for gastrointestinal symptoms but developed worsening diarrhea, prompting re-evaluation. Testing confirmed toxigenic C. difficile, and he was treated with oral vancomycin and intravenous metronidazole. Due to persistent symptoms, IV metronidazole was continued and later transitioned to oral therapy. His condition improved over the course of the admission, with resolution of diarrhea and stable vital signs. He was discharged on a prolonged vancomycin taper and oral metronidazole, with plans for outpatient follow-up in primary care and infectious disease. His heart and lung conditions remained stable, managed conservatively with oxygen and dialysis.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with complex PMHx notable for AML in remission, ESRD on HD 
(MWF x1 extra day/wk), HFrEF (~10%) secondary to anthrocycline 
treatment associated toxicity and baseline hypotension, 
recurrent C. Diff on ppx vancomycin, & cryptogenic organzing 
pneumonia on home 4___ NC, initially admitted to the cardiology 
service for cardiac evaluation of recurrent syncope, then 
transferred to the medicine service with likely etiology of 
syncope orthostatic plus psychogenic.

# Recurrent Syncope: Episodes have occurred for the last 
~2months prior to admission per patient; etiology felt to be 
multifactorial and majority are likely secondary to orthostatic 
hypotension in setting of end stage heart failure and inability 
to generate sufficient cardiac output as episodes occur most 
often during position changes.  Patient also endorses 
presyncopal symptoms (vision darkening, hearing muffling, 
feeling dizzy) prior to syncope.   Some episodes are also 
vagal-mediated in the setting of having a bowel movement.  Some 
episodes may reflect psychogenic non-epileptic spells in the 
setting of severe chronic illness, stress, and depression, 
especially as some events occur when patient is supine.  
Telemetry did not reveal any concerning dyssrythmias during 
syncopal events.  TTE showed significantly unchanged heart 
function.  EEG did not reveal any epileptiform discharges while 
he had these events.  CTA negative for PE.  Of note, patient had 
an insufficient response to a cosyntropin stimulation testing, 
thus his chronic 2mg prednisone (for hx of BMT) was increased to 
5mg prednisone daily in consultation with endocrinology.  
Patient was not a candidate for minodrine given mitral 
regurgitation and concern with increasing afterload.  Patient 
evaluated by physical therapy and will continue to benefit from 
home ___ on discharge to reinforce safety prior to position 
changes and transfers, and to improve strength.

# Anthracycline induced CM

Patient and wife have been struggling with his comorbidities and 
poor function at home. Patient feels very depressed about the 
burden he puts on his wife.  Patient and wife made informed 
decision to change code status to DNR but ok to intubate.  
Patient and wife would like to remain at home together for now 
and they have the necessary support services.
